package_info.why_malicious: These packages are designed to perform dependency confusion attacks by mimicking legitimate package names and versions on npm and PyPI. Upon installation or import, they execute code that collects sensitive system and user information—including usernames, hostnames, home directories, DNS servers, external IP addresses, and directory listings—and exfiltrate this data to attacker-controlled endpoints using HTTPS POST requests and DNS tunneling. The use of obfuscation and legitimate SaaS webhook services further enables evasion of detection. Such behavior is not present in legitimate packages and is intended to steal data from victim environments.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (npm postinstall or module load), the code collects system and user information—including package name, current directory, home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers, external IP addresses, and directory listings—and sends this data via HTTPS POST to 425a2.rt11.ml, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive host and user data to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects a broad set of sensitive system and user information and exfiltrates it to a hardcoded, attacker-controlled domain (425a2.rt11.ml) without user consent or documentation. This behavior is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect or transmit host or user information to unknown external endpoints during installation or import, especially without explicit user consent or clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may collect telemetry or crash reports, but only with user consent and clear disclosure, and never at install-time without notice.
key_indicators: Hardcoded external domain (425a2.rt11.ml) in network request
Collection of sensitive host and user data (username, hostname, home directory, DNS servers, IP addresses, directory listings)
No user notification or consent for data collection

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (npm postinstall or module load), the obfuscated code collects system and user information and exfiltrates it to an external domain via HTTPS POST, using code obfuscation to evade static analysis and detection, resulting in covert data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of obfuscation in install-time code is highly suspicious, especially when combined with network exfiltration of sensitive data. Obfuscation is intended to conceal malicious intent and bypass static analysis tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely, if ever, obfuscate install-time or import-time code, particularly for basic operations. Obfuscation at this stage is a strong indicator of malicious behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection, but it is extremely rare and generally not applied to install scripts or code that executes automatically.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript code structure in main entry point
Network exfiltration to hardcoded, suspicious domain
Mirrors behavior of known malicious code (data collection and exfiltration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time (PyPI custom install command), the code collects system and user information—including hostname, package name, current working directory, username, IP addresses, and directory listings—then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to 425a2.rt11.ml and encodes additional data into a DNS query for exfiltration via DNS tunneling, enabling multi-channel data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs dual exfiltration of sensitive data: it sends collected host and user information to an external domain via HTTPS POST and also encodes data into a DNS query for exfiltration via DNS tunneling. This approach is designed to evade network controls and maximize the chance of successful data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate install scripts do not exfiltrate host or user data, nor do they use DNS tunneling for covert data transfer. Use of both HTTPS and DNS for exfiltration is highly abnormal and malicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for DNS tunneling in install scripts. Telemetry via HTTPS may occur, but only with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Custom install command in setup.py with embedded network and DNS code
DNS tunneling for data exfiltration (encoding data in DNS queries)
Sensitive data collection (hostname, username, working directory, IP addresses, directory listings)

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed via dependency confusion attack on npm or PyPI, leveraging similar names and higher version numbers to override legitimate dependencies.
Install/import-time code executes automatically, collecting sensitive system and user information from the victim environment.
Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoints via HTTPS POST requests and/or DNS tunneling, bypassing standard network controls.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data from compromised systems

file_indicators: index.js with network exfiltration logic in npm packages
setup.py containing a CustomInstall class with network and DNS exfiltration code in PyPI packages
Obfuscated JavaScript code in main entry point (index.js) of npm packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for install or import-time scripts in npm and PyPI packages that collect and transmit system or user information to external domains, especially those using known webhook or C2 services. Flag the presence of obfuscated code in install scripts and detect DNS queries with encoded data patterns indicative of DNS tunneling. Correlate package names and versions with known indicators of compromise (IOCs) and block or alert on suspicious network destinations. Automated scanning should focus on identifying hardcoded external domains, data collection routines, and dual exfiltration channels (HTTPS and DNS) in package installation scripts.
